title: Rhyme Circle: Listen, Match, Invent
subject: Phonological awareness
objective: With adult support, recognize and generate spoken rhymes.
publicationStatus: Private draft — awaiting Katia’s publication approval; not for sale.
thumbnailAlt: Official KSP Haitian-flag book logo above Rhyme Circle: Listen, Match, Invent; Pre-K • Massachusetts • Phonological awareness; private draft cover.
summary: With adult support, recognize and generate spoken rhymes. Includes models, practice, exit check, and answer guidance.
detailedDescription: Rhyme Circle: Listen, Match, Invent gives Pre-K learners a focused route from explicit modeling to supported practice and independent application. A rhyme has the same ending sound, even when its spelling differs. Say each pair naturally, then stretch the ending. Children may answer by speaking, pointing to a yes/no card, or giving a thumbs signal. Adults read every word; printed-word reading is not expected. Accept a playful invented word if its ending genuinely rhymes, then model a real word. Use four prompts per sitting.
included: 4 teacher answer-key pages covering all 20 tasks
minutes: Four 8–12-minute supported sessions and a 5-minute oral check.
studentDirections: Listen to the adult, then speak, point, draw, or act your response. Ask to hear the words or story again.
teacherUse: Model the two examples; use tasks 1–4 as a readiness check. Assign four tasks per practice block, then use the independent exit responses to select a specific reteaching move. For extended writing, supply separate paper. Keep answer pages separate.
answerKey: Answers or explicit acceptable-response criteria for all 20 tasks; two explained models; local 0–2-per-task exit rubric. Open-ended answers allow justified alternatives.

differentiation.AIG: Ask the learner to invent a new rhyme pair or retell from another character’s view; explain the choice.
differentiation.504: Follow the individual plan: breaks, enlarged print, extra time, reduced copying, or an alternative response method as documented. These are classroom options, not a statement of permitted test accommodations.
differentiation.EC: Read all directions and stories aloud; model one response; use gestures, pictures drawn by the learner, or AAC. Record exact responses without demanding writing.
differentiation.ESL: Explain word meanings with gestures before rhyme listening. Invite home-language retelling first; compare the target English sounds without judging accent.

summary: Read common sh and ch consonant digraphs in words and short sentences. Includes models, practice, exit check, and answer guidance.
detailedDescription: Two Letters, One Sound: SH and CH Workshop gives Grade 1 learners a focused route from explicit modeling to supported practice and independent application. detailedDescription: Word Jobs: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives, and Adverbs gives Grade 3 learners a focused route from explicit modeling to supported practice and independent application. Ask what the word does here, not just what ending it has. This packet uses clear examples, not all possible word jobs.

4 teacher answer-key pages covering all 20 tasks
minutes: Two 30–40-minute sessions plus a 10–15-minute exit check; extended writing or speech rehearsal may take longer.
studentDirections: Read the lesson and supplied text or reference. Attempt each task before viewing the key. Explain when asked. Use separate paper for full drafts or longer answers; the PDF is not a fillable form.
teacherUse: Model the two examples; use tasks 1–4 as a readiness check. Assign four tasks per practice block, then use the independent exit responses to select a specific reteaching move. For extended writing, supply separate paper. Keep answer pages separate.
answerKey: Answers or explicit acceptable-response criteria for all 20 tasks; two explained models; local 0–2-per-task exit rubric. Open-ended answers allow justified alternatives.

differentiation.AIG: Ask for a counterexample, an alternative supported interpretation, or a newly written item with an explanation. Add depth rather than speed.
differentiation.504: Follow the individual plan: breaks, enlarged print, extra time, reduced copying, or an alternative response method as documented. These are classroom options, not a statement of permitted test accommodations.
differentiation.EC: Follow the IEP; show one task at a time, model the first decision, and permit dictated reasoning when appropriate. For decoding practice, distinguish an adult-read direction from an adult-read target word.
differentiation.ESL: Preview task verbs and key vocabulary, allow home-language planning, and offer “My answer is ___ because ___.” Evaluate the targeted skill separately from unrelated language errors. For French, retain the target French sentence while explaining directions in a familiar language.

preparation: Print the selected pages; provide pencil and extra paper. Read the teacher guide and prerequisite vocabulary. Adult facilitation is required for Pre-K/Kindergarten. No outside novel, paid app, or external passage required.
printing: US Letter, actual size; print student pages separately from keys. Color branding remains legible in grayscale.
digitalUse: Selectable-text PDF for viewing or optional annotation; not a fillable form or certified tagged PDF. Use only a restricted classroom LMS.
license: Single teacher and their own students; private classroom/LMS use. No resale, public redistribution, or sharing of complete files.
originalContent: All student passages, practice tasks, model explanations, and answer guidance are original. No released questions or branded curriculum copied. Official logo reused unchanged.
